speaker: Doctor
text: Given the triad of gait disturbance, urinary incontinence, and cognitive/communication changes, I need to rule out normal pressure hydrocephalus. Have you noticed any significant decline in your memory or thinking abilities over the same period?

text: My main symptom is Progressive difficulty walking. I also have Urinary incontinence, Slurred speech, Rigidity in limbs, Mild hand tremor, Orthostatic hypotension.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of parkinsonism, autonomic dysfunction, and early bulbar signs strongly suggests Multiple System Atrophy. REQUEST TEST: Brain MRI.

text: RESULTS: Multiple areas of atrophy and signal changes in the brainstem, cerebellum, and basal ganglia, consistent with neurodegenerative processes.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI findings of brainstem and cerebellar atrophy, combined with your parkinsonian symptoms and autonomic instability, strongly point to Multiple System Atrophy. Do you experience any significant episodes of fainting or dizziness when you stand up quickly?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Unremarkable. No known chronic diseases. Social history: Occasionally consumes alcohol. Non-smoker. Works as a bank clerk.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the history; your unremarkable past medical history helps rule out secondary causes like vascular parkinsonism.
